correctness.rationale: For every q>=2,n>=3 the circular support gap d is invariant under admissible shift. Each component contracts to the bidirected complete bipartite digraph on 2(q-1) junctions or (when n is even and d=n/2) the complete digraph with loops on q-1 junctions. Directed Matrix-Tree gives cofactors s^(2s-2) and s^(s-2) (s>1; s=1 handled separately); BEST gives A_s and B_s. Exactly floor(n/2) disjoint components force that many tracks, and independent tours give the claimed product. All boundary cases and rotations are specified. A standalone exact integer checker reconstructed 31 components and directly enumerated fixed-first-edge tours for selected cases; finite checks corroborate the proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement counts the complete family of minimum circular covers of the full-length exactly-two-nonzero language, with exact gap-resolved numbers. The 2012 fixed-weight shorthand construction and 2026 bounded-weight universal cycles do not imply the disjoint-component BEST enumerators or the minimum-cover product; own adjacent-weight and sparse/dense enumerations are likewise different. Actual semantic-index and source searches were performed. An inaccessible related preprint and unindexed prior work remain explicit priority risks.

value.rationale: For strict full-length exact-weight-two languages the known one-track obstruction makes minimum cyclic track covers a natural missing invariant. The theorem gives the least track count, complete all-alphabet and all-length multiplicities, gap-specific circuit sizes and exact antipodal transition. Its strong reduction to complete bipartite versus looped complete digraph is structural; the formula counts every optimal design rather than producing an arbitrary code or a single example.
